factorRatings.note: The Stranger found the custom pies merely on par with other Seattle pizzerias but singled out house specialty pies -- the pepperoni-pineapple-jalapeño Staple & Fancy, the mushroom-and-sage Funghi -- as worth the trip; The Infatuation praises the daily rotating slices as near NY-caliber, calling the place 'awesome.'

The Infatuation calls it a decent, unspectacular NY-style slice joint good for a late-night pepperoni slice; Seattle Spectator's by-the-slice roundup dinged it for a greasy, soggy base despite a crunchier-than-average crust.

The Infatuation rates it among the city's best, praising crunchy-but-not-burnt crusts and calling its 3 Cheese pie 'the greatest white pizza in town'; Seattle Refined highlights the naturally leavened dough and handmade pasta since the Capitol Hill original opened in 2020.

The Infatuation calls it 'as close to perfect as a restaurant gets,' and The Stranger describes an apple-wood-fired crust that's blackened and bubbly at the edge yet thin and pliant at the center, built from a wetter, saltier dough than most Seattle pizzerias use.

The Infatuation praises a thick, crunchy crust charred nearly black on the bottom, and The Stranger's slice face-off named it the city's top pick for New Jersey-style square Sicilian slices with crispy, golden-brown cheese edges.

The Infatuation rates it a middling 'it's fine,' saying only the pesto slice is worth ordering while the red slices taste of 'pretty much nothing'; Seattle Spectator likewise found the slice greasy and structurally weak, though praised its six-inch cheese pull.

The Infatuation calls the pizzas excellent and the setting 'as Pacific Northwest as it gets,' citing the margherita, a hearty whole hog pie, and a smoked eggplant pie for vegetarians, with eggs from an on-site chicken coop topping the arugula pie.
